text: Working with APIs is an important skill for modern developers. An API allows two programs to communicate with each other. Usually, your application sends an HTTP request to a server, and the server sends back a response. This response often contains data in JSON format, which is easy to read and use. Before you can access most APIs, you need authentication, such as an API key, to prove who you are. You should also be careful with rate limits, because APIs often allow only a limited number of requests per minute. Finally, always add error handling to your code, so your app can react properly when something goes wrong.
